text: A sentence devoid of expectation (ākāṅkṣā) and other factors is not a valid means of knowledge. For example, the statement “The white horse is a man, an elephant” is not a valid means of knowledge due to the absence of expectation. Similarly, the command “Wash with fire” is not a valid means of knowledge due to the absence of fitness (yogyatā). And words such as “Strike! Strike! Bring the cows!” are not valid means of knowledge due to the absence of proximity (sannidhi). || 50 ||
